short: Relax in Bao Bao’s Cozy Laundromat, an idle game where you join Bao Bao, a charming panda, in creating the coziest laundromat. Purchase colorful washing machines, add delightful decorations, and hire panda helpers. Watch your cozy laundromat bustle with life, even when you’re not around!
about: Step into the warm and welcoming world of Bao Bao's Cozy Laundromat, where our lovable panda, Bao Bao, is eager to share her dream with you. Starting with just 500💰, you'll help Bao Bao transform a humble beginning into a bustling haven of cleanliness and charm. Picture rows of vibrant, colorful washing machines humming gently, alongside dryers that turn laundry day into a soothing ritual. But it’s not just about washing clothes—it's about creating a space that feels like home.             As you and Bao Bao work together, you'll have the chance to add all sorts of delightful touches: cozy furniture where customers can relax with a good book, snack-filled vending machines that bring joy to those waiting, and lush, leafy plants that breathe life into every corner. And because no great venture is ever truly solo, you'll soon be able to welcome other panda friends to join the fun, each bringing their own special touch to the laundromat.  What's even more relaxing is that Bao Bao's Cozy Laundromat is an idle game, meaning you can let it run peacefully in the background without needing too much interaction. Your laundromat will keep thriving, even when you're off doing other things, allowing you to return to a bustling, cozy environment whenever you're ready.           To make the experience even more serene, you'll be surrounded by the gentle sounds of 10 beautiful lo-fi soundtracks, creating the perfect atmosphere for a cozy, laid-back experience. Let the music soothe your soul as you help Bao Bao build her dream.          So come on in, take a deep breath, and feel the warmth of Bao Bao's Cozy Laundromat wrap around you like a favorite blanket. Together, you'll create a place that’s not just about doing laundry—it’s about finding a little bit of peace, happiness, and sweet melodies in the everyday. Focus on work, browse the web, or watch a video, then return to make the decisions that matter: adjust your lineup, equip new gear, unlock talents, and send the journey onward. Roles, races, elements, skills, innate affixes, and synergies all interact. Protect your main damage dealer, combine skill effects, or build an entire lineup around a favorite Dreamspirit—every adjustment can take your team farther.          · Step Away. The Battle Continues.  Your team automatically fights enemies, uses skills, and advances through stages. Even while you are away, it continues earning offline rewards. Every reward and every choice changes where your team goes next.          · Journey Deeper into the Dream  Challenge 5 map floors, 4 difficulty levels, and 200 stage combinations. Hunt for better equipment, hatch rarer Dreamspirits, and keep perfecting your three-member team.   Build your team. Adventure automatically. Keep dreaming.

name: WinMon
lang: English*, Vietnamese*, Russian*, Simplified Chinese*, Japanese*, German*, Korean*, Traditional Chinese**
short: Feed your cute little monsters, then put them to work. No breaks, no unions, no mercy. Keep them productive long enough and your adorable workforce won't stay little: overfed and overworked, they'll swell into towering, monstrous beasts. Capitalism has never looked so squishy.
about: Welcome to WinMon Inc. Where Cute Meets Quota.   Somewhere between a farm and a startup, your desktop just became a workplace. WinMons are small, squishy, and disturbingly loyal. Feed them, and they'll do anything for you. Anything. That's not a warning, that's the business model.  There is no HR department. There is no lunch break. There is only the mission: keep them fed, keep them working, and watch the numbers go up.           Hire Cute. Work Them Harder.   Every WinMon comes preloaded with a job title and zero say in the matter. Eight professions, eight ways to be useful:    Seeder, sows seeds onto your plantations    Waterer, keeps the crops and water machines running    Lighter, provides heat and light for the thermal work    Miner, breaks down ore so somebody else can use it    Lumberjack, gathers the wood nobody thanked them for    Builder, the only one who actually gets to build anything    Engineer, runs everything that needs electricity    Alchemist, cooks the food and crafts the magic, on schedule    Around them, build an operation of nearly 30 machines and buildings: plantations, magic trees, waterpumps, electric factories, cooking pots for every occasion, even a Fusion Core you dig out of an abandoned ruin and repair, purely so you can fuse WinMons together into "ultimate lifeforms." Nobody in HR would sign off on that. There is no HR.           Keep Them Fed. Keep Them Growing.   Here's the part corporate doesn't put in the brochure: what you feed them doesn't just keep them alive, it changes them. Let a WinMon consume enough of what it produces and it stops being small. It stops being cute. It evolves, and your once-adorable little laborer starts putting on size, muscle, and an unsettling number of teeth.  With so many unique forms across 31 evolution lines (base, Stage 2, Stage 3), 8 elements, 5 power tiers, 4 quality grades, and 19 personality traits that range from Lazy all the way up to Mythic-grade Superhuman, there is a lot of room for a small worker to become a very large problem.  Congratulations. You built a monopoly, and also several actual monsters.            Skill Up. Then Watch It Turn.    Invest in 52 skill nodes to speed up production, expand your storage, and generally optimize the workforce. Then push into Prestige, 28 more nodes deep, and unlock the endgame Revolution system: a genuinely harder second run where the Pig King, the fattest cat in the building, finally turns on your WinMons himself.  Turns out exploitation doesn't stop at the top. It just changes who's holding the whip.  Feed the machine. Grow the empire. Try not to think too hard about what "growth" really means here.  As your WinMons work and produce items, they’ll consume the items they make to evolve into stronger, rarer forms with higher working capability, slowly turning your army into a fashion show of cool WinMons.

name: Little LUMI Model
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese
short: Lumi moves onto your desktop and stays there. She walks your taskbar, climbs the window you are typing in, hangs from title bars and naps when nothing happens. Pat her head, turn on focus mode, let her shout your alarms, summon more Lumis, or grab new characters on the Workshop. All hand-drawn.
about: Lumi moves in   Little LUMI Model puts Lumi on your screen and lets her live there. She walks along the bottom of your monitor, climbs the side of the window you are typing in, hangs from your title bars, and sits down for a nap when nothing is happening.  She is simply there, doing her own thing, while you work.   What she does      Walks, runs, sprints, skids.  Full-speed dashes that stop with a puff of dust.     Treats your desktop as terrain.  Walls, ceilings, window edges, window faces — and she will dive off a title bar for no reason at all.     Never quite idle.  Head tilts, humming with floating notes, little hops, sitting down and looking around, the occasional mumble to herself.     When a credit drops from the sky  she notices, runs over, and picks it up with a chime.    64 behaviours run on 122 frames, every one of them drawn by hand.   Reacts to you      Pat her head.  Rub the top of her head with the mouse; the cursor turns into a hand and Lumi lights up.     Pick her up, shake her, throw her across the screen.  Click once and she says hello.     Takes requests.  Right-click for a specific action, or call her to your cursor from the tray icon.     What grows over time      Affection.  Days spent together and head pats add up through six stages, each unlocking new things for her to mumble.     50 Steam achievements.  From the first hello to the thousandth credit.     Quiet while you work      Focus mode.  One right-click and Lumi settles down. Turn on the Pomodoro timer and she moves between focus and break on her own.     Alarms.  When the time comes she sounds a siren and runs around the floor for a minute so you cannot miss it. She can also call out the hour.     Favours.  Register something you do often, like showing the desktop, and Lumi will hop and do it for you when asked.     Hides on her own in front of full-screen apps.  No interruptions during games or screen sharing.     Comes in numbers   Summon as many Lumis as your desktop can hold. With two or more they chat, high-five, share credits, march in a line, gather on call, and play tag.   Optional extras   Off by default, but there are special features you can switch on.     Bongo Lumi mode.  A desk-bound Lumi sits in the corner and hits the bongos every time you type or move the mouse.     Floating Garden.  Draw islands and ladders on your screen and Lumi walks them, climbs them, and settles on top.     Pythagoras game.  Place platforms, trampolines, walls and ladders to send Lumi to the goal.     Window toss.  Lumi picks up a window and throws it off the screen.     Workshop   Subscribe to a character someone else drew on the Steam Workshop and it walks the desktop next to Lumi.   Built to be left alone      Nothing to install.  The Java runtime ships inside. No separate download, no account, no internet connection.     Quiet by default.  No launcher, no login, no notifications, no background service. Notifications only happen if you turn them on.     You choose her playground.  Pick which applications she is allowed to climb.     Five languages.  Korean, English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese. Multiple monitors and display scaling are supported.

name: Sill Cats
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Ukrainian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Russian, Italian, Indonesian, Dutch, Greek, Swedish, Spanish - Latin America, Thai, Czech, Danish, Norwegian, Hungarian, Finnish, Bulgarian, Polish, Romanian, Arabic, Malay
short: Tiny cats have moved into your desktop. They pad around the screen, bat at your cursor, curl up to sleep somewhere, and suddenly break into a sprint in the middle of the night. Dote on their delightfully cat-like antics. Adopt two cats for free.
about: Sill Cats is an always-on desktop app in which tiny cats move into your computer's desktop.   They pad along the tops of your open windows, curl up and sleep soundly in some corner, and perk up—"what's that?"—when your mouse moves. At 2 in the morning they'll suddenly tear across the screen at full speed. Yes, they really do get the zoomies. If you've ever had a cat, you'll probably just get it.        What these cats are like    The whole desktop is their walking course — they stroll leisurely all over your desktop    Jumping onto windows — they explore your workspace as they please     Curious about the cursor — when the mouse moves, they might quietly sidle up… or might not    Click to play with them — one click to catch their eye, two for a reaction, three and they just might actually play with you    Their mood shifts with the time of day — liveliest at dawn and dusk, and utterly lazy at midday (this is what's called being "crepuscular")    Late-night zoomies — a sudden sprint around 1–4 a.m.; count yourself lucky to catch it     Fine with a big screen — no matter how many monitors you have, every one becomes part of the cats' walking course    They usually stay out of your way, but every now and then they'll bat at your cursor. Please cut them some slack there. They're cats, after all.    If you find a cat you love, give it a name and make it your very own.           Adopt two cats for free  Sill Cats is free to start. The first two you can adopt are a sleek Abyssinian and a dashing Tuxedo. Once you're smitten, you can grow the family through breed packs. Even mulling over which one to welcome first is part of the fun.  By default, two cats are shown on screen. If you'd like just one, click the cat signboard, or right-click the icon in the Windows system tray to open the settings menu, and change it under "Number of Cats."    About additional cats  Purchasing DLC adds more cat looks and breeds you can choose from.    DLC adds the cat looks and breeds you can choose from.   It does not raise the maximum number of cats that can appear on screen at once.    Sill Cats also offers a variety of cat toy DLCs to liven up your screen.  There's a free "Basic Toy Pack" as well, so please start there.    How to set things up  Changing the cat breed, quitting the app, and adjusting the various settings are all done from the settings menu.   Click the cat signboard, or right-click the Sill Cats icon in the system tray, to open the settings menu.   If you can't find the icon, check the hidden icons via the "^" button at the bottom-right of the screen.  Up to two cats can be shown at once.  ※ If you spot a bug, it would be a great help if you reported it on the discussion boards in the "Community Hub."    About the Free Toy Pack  Among the DLCs, there is a free Toy Pack: the "Basic Toy Pack." It lets you place cat toys on your screen for free, so please be sure to download it. We'll keep updating the free Toy Pack little by little and adding more toys.    Development roadmap  We have the following updates planned going forward.   【Feature additions】   ・Adding more cat toys  ・Adding more cat gestures  ・Adding more cat breeds  ・Adding a feature to pet the cats  and more    ※ Planned content may change depending on the state of development. ※ More detailed plans are announced on the discussion boards in the Community Hub.  Streaming policy  You are free to stream and post videos of this game, monetized or not. No prior permission or notice is required.  You don't have to tell us, but we'd be delighted if you did. A heads-up on Discord or X (formerly Twitter) is a big help. You can find our Discord and X accounts from the store page. We'd also be thrilled if you put the store page URL in your stream or video description. If we know ahead of time, we may be able to help promote your stream.  That said, please refrain from streams that fall under any of the following:  ・Il

name: Professor Simulator: Desktop Lab
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese
short: Professor Simulator: Desktop Lab is a semi-idle desktop simulation game about academic life. Keep a tiny lab in the corner of your screen while you work, study, or relax. Recruit graduate students, apply for research projects, publish papers, purchase equipment, and build your own research team.
about: This is an idle game that won’t interrupt your work, experiments, or paper writing.  It only takes up a tiny corner of your screen, quietly running in the background and keeping you company.  In the game, you play as a young lecturer at the start of your academic career. Beginning with a humble little lab, you will recruit students, conduct research projects, publish papers, purchase equipment, set lab rules, and gradually climb the academic ladder until you become a true academic heavyweight.  The journey may be painful, and it may be absurd, but at least—  you finally get to be the advisor.      Interview Students      Starting from scratch, you will personally interview master’s and PhD students, selecting the most suitable candidates to join your team.  Different students have different abilities, personalities, and growth potential. Some are naturally gifted, some are hardworking and reliable, and some look extremely promising—while simply waiting for the perfect chance to slack off.  As your academic rank rises, your lab will gradually expand, allowing you to recruit more students and build a larger research team.                Manage Your Research Team      Students will occasionally “slack off,” so you need to check in regularly, click to view their status, motivate them, boost their research abilities, and effectively reduce the number of times they secretly “take it easy.”          You can observe each student’s condition, ability growth, stress, and relationships, then train them, assign tasks, or let them continue experiencing the harsh reality of academia at the right moment.          If a student produces little to no results for a long time... you also have the authority to take decisive action—deny graduation and let them feel the full force of the “academic iron fist.”          Of course, once you are promoted to a higher academic rank, your management options will become even richer. The lab rules system allows you to adjust stipends, authorship rules, and graduation requirements, creating a research environment that is lenient, strict, or full of pressure.        Conduct Projects and Publish Papers      Research cannot rely on passion alone. You also need projects and results.  Lead your students through different types of research projects, accumulating innovation, workload, and writing quality. When the results are ready, remember to write the paper and submit it to a journal.  The higher the quality of your work, the greater the chance of being accepted by a high-impact journal. But submission is never entirely predictable—even if you do everything well, you still may not escape the fate assigned by the reviewers.          You will need to guide your students through different research stages, bouncing between revisions, rejections, and publications, eventually accumulating academic influence of your own. Different equipment affects research outputs such as innovation, workload, and writing quality. Based on the needs of your current projects, you can gradually add research instruments, daily-use facilities, and decorations, transforming your once modest lab into a high-end, intelligent, and perhaps slightly absurd modern research platform.  At the same time, do not forget to add some entertainment and daily-life facilities to relieve the students’ accumulated stress and prevent their depression index from skyrocketing.                Climb the Academic Ladder      As your influence grows, you will gradually be promoted through academic ranks.  Starting as a lecturer, you will rise to associate professor, professor, and even higher levels of academic leadership. There are 9 advisor ranks in total, and your lab size, student capacity, and available projects will all expand as you advance.          Becoming a professor is not the end. name: Lootborne
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Thai, Polish, Turkish
short: A challenging dark fantasy idle RPG that lives in the corner of your screen. Fight and loot while you work, refine your build, trigger item synergies, and grow stronger. An autobattler with asynchronous PvP, for glory and loot!
about: Battle while you work  Lootborne runs in a window small enough to sit next to whatever you are actually doing. With the optional “always on top” setting, your hero keeps fighting and looting on its own, for as long as stamina holds... then rests and goes again. You look over when you decide it’s time to level up or update your gear.  Drop loot and forge items  424 items across six rarities. Start with battered gear and claw your way toward magic rings, cursed blades, ancient tomes, and mythic artifacts that can redefine your run. Gear up not only for power, but for aesthetics too. And when a duplicate drops, throw it into the forge and gamble it upward.              Elements, Perks, and Potions  Arcane, Flame, Frost, Holy, Shadow. Items carry elemental affinities that stack into synergies; 26 Perks change how your character fights, and 25 Potions let you tilt a fight you are losing. Stats can be respecced: an early mistake is not a dead character.              Challenge other players in async PvP  Your build is not limited to PvE. Test it against other players’ builds in asynchronous battles: no lobby, no queue, no waiting. And it does not stop when you close the game, as challenges can resolve even while you're not playing, with the results waiting when you come back.  Climb the global ladder, challenge your Steam friends, and hunt four PvP bosses that drop gear you cannot get anywhere else.               Trade on the Steam Market  We consider this a feature of the game, not a reason to play it.  For this reason, we’ve added some limits and safeguards:    The Steam Market opens one week after release.    Rare and Epic items, together with Legendary items dropped in battle, can be traded with other players on the Steam Community Market for Steam Wallet funds.    Common, Mythic, and Ascended items are account-bound, along with forged Legendary items. These cannot be traded.    Trading unlocks at level 15 on an account that is at least 7 days old. You can mark up to 20 items as sellable per week, with a maximum of 4 per day.                Fair Play & Ban Policy  A fair, healthy game environment matters to us, and what we learned during the demo shaped how we handle bots and cheaters.    Anti-cheat runs server-side.    We never monitor or scan other apps or processes on your PC. Not to detect cheating or for any other reason.    Depending on the violation, we may restrict access to leaderboards, trading, and matchmaking, or ban the account from the game, but we never request a Steam-level (VAC/Game) ban.    Balance and economy changes are always disclosed in patch notes, never applied silently.    Think you were flagged by mistake? Appeal anytime at our support email. We acknowledge appeals within 72 hours and resolve them within 14 days (we're still a small indie team after all). If we got it wrong, we fully restore what was affected and compensate you on top of it.    You can report cheaters on our Discord or via email.      Offline Play & Data Gathering    PvE is fully playable offline, no connection required, though stamina paces the run either way. Only PvP, trading, and leaderboards require you to be online.    We collect gameplay data, never personal data, to help us improve the game and spot cheaters. You can opt out anytime in Settings.

short: Desktop Rave is a rhythm/idle/incremental desktop companion that turns the music you play on Windows into game resources! Like Bongo cat but with each beat of your music playing on Windows!
about: 🎧 You are the DJ of your own club! They dance to whatever music you're playing and earn resources with each beat.  🎵 Support any music player/browser on Windows, Apple Music/Spotify/Chrome/Firefox anything goes.  🤖 All the art assets were hand made by human, 0% AI assets involved.                   ✨ Key Features:      Idle/Incremental Gameplay:  The club generates resource with each beat that can be used to upgrade and expand.     Free Placement:  You can scale/move/rotate the game view and place wherever suit you the best on the Desktop.     Full Customization:  You can build and customize the lighting/layout/shape of your own unique club.                     💻 Built for the Background  Very low performance overhead when running in the background  🎛️  Light sensitivity options:  All lighting effects can be dimmed, and flashing effects can be slowed down.  🤓 Linux Support:  With GE-Proton11-9 and launch option set to:"WINE_LAYERED_OVERLAY_ALPHA=1 %command%", shut-out to the community member who discovered it❤️     Q&A:    Does the game record my audio or send it to a server for processing?  No. This is a single player game that runs without a server or internet connection. All audio data is processed locally in real time and discarded immediately.     Does the game know what I’m listening to?  The game only analyzes audio frequencies and amplitudes, for example: an amplitude of 0.7 in the 50–250 Hz frequency band.     Does the game work with any music player or browser?  Yes. The game listens to your Windows audio output, so you can use any music player or browser. Apple Music, Spotify, SoundCloud, and YouTube all work, including playback through browsers such as Chrome and Firefox.     Does the game work with any music genre? What about slow music?  Yes. The game works with any music genre. Certain perks in the skill tree compensate for slower music.     Privacy (Steam Windows)   This game may read your Steam country code once at boot to choose consent rules. That code is not saved and is not sent to a developer server. If Steam country is unavailable, the game treats location as unknown and asks before optional statistics.  If allowed by regional policy or your consent, the game may send optional gameplay analytics to GameAnalytics (build/version, an anonymous save-slot id that is never reused after deletion, playtime on that save, and economy, tutorial, building, and Club Promo actions). It does not send Steam account ids, save names, song titles, or grid positions. It may also write coarse lifetime totals through Steam UserStats, linked to your Steam account. Analytics are not required to play, are not sold, and are not used for ads. Unity Analytics and Unity Ads are disabled.  You can allow or deny this at the boot prompt (protected/unknown regions) and later in Settings → Privacy. Turning it off stops future sends. The game cannot delete data GameAnalytics or Steam already hold. Use this page’s support email for privacy questions.  Unity Diagnostics separately sends crash and exception reports, device and software details, session information, and an installation ID to Unity to investigate errors and improve stability. This reporting can start before your analytics consent choice and continues if you decline analytics or the age affirmation, or turn off Gameplay analytics in Settings → Privacy. There is no in-game opt-out for Diagnostics. Unity documents a default 90-day retention period for Diagnostics personal data. Use this page’s support email for privacy questions or access/deletion requests. Requests for a specific installation require its Unity installation ID.  Club saves and slot previews can sync through Steam Cloud (download on launch, upload on exit). Dynamic Cloud Sync is not used. Device preferences (audio, graphics, privacy, etc.) stay on this PC and do not sync. The game is not directed at children under 13.

Run it as a thin strip at the bottom of your screen, menus open right above it. Play  Goblin Attack  in full screen or switch to a mode designed to  sit at the bottom of your screen  just like those games you keep running in the background. Your gold and passive income keep flowing while you work, browse, or watch something. Your progress never stops.                You start as a humble walking archer. Tap to shoot, earn gold, and grow. Unlock a  Mounted Archer , then a  Cart with two archers , then a  bigger cart with four , and finally a  Walking Tower  armed with seven archers that even handles melee automatically. Then  Ascend : reset your progress, keep your  Essence , and unlock powerful new abilities like  Rain of Arrows  or  multi-shot on tap . Each reset gets you stronger than before.       As you move forward, goblins appear in your path.  Most go down in one shot.  Shield Bearers  take several hits depending on their size.  Tank Goblins  are massive and absorb a lot before falling. name: Idle Knight
lang: English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Czech, Simplified Chinese, Russian
short: Idle Knight turns your clicks, keystrokes, and controller inputs into XP while it runs in the background. Use your PC, grow your knight, build your character, collect skins, open hourly chests, clear dungeons, and climb the ranks.
about: Use your PC. Grow your knight.      Idle Knight  is an idle RPG that runs in the background while you use your computer.  Every real interaction helps your knight progress. Mouse clicks, keyboard inputs and controller actions generate XP.  Use your PC normally and let your knight grow alongside you.  Work, study, browse the web, watch videos, play another game or simply use your computer. Your knight keeps progressing in the background.         YOUR PC. YOUR PROGRESSION.     The concept is simple.    You don't need to actively grind the game. Your normal PC activity generates XP for your knight.  Level up, earn stat points, improve your build and become stronger.  Early progression is fast and rewarding. As you progress further, optimization becomes more important.  Your goal isn't just to gain levels. It's to build a character capable of pushing further.         BUILD YOUR KNIGHT     Every level gives you stat points that shape your character.     HP   Increase your survivability.   DMG   Deal more damage and defeat enemies faster.   AGI   Improve your speed and evasion.    Choose the build that fits your playstyle.  Focus on damage, build a tank, specialize in agility or create your own hybrid build.  There is no single perfect build. Different choices can be useful depending on your goals.         EXPERIMENT AND OPTIMIZE      You are not permanently locked into your choices.            Special items such as the  Phoenix Feather  allow you to reset your stats while keeping your level.  Try different builds, test your stats and find the setup that works best for you.         DUNGEONS              Enter dungeons and put your build to the test.  Choose a dungeon based on its recommended level, fight through multiple floors and face the final boss.  Higher difficulty means greater challenges and better rewards.  A weak build can struggle before reaching the end.  A well-optimized build can clear dungeons efficiently and push further.         CLIMB THE RANKS                           Compete in ranked mode and see how far your build can take you.   Farmer -> Stable Boy -> Infantryman -> Knight -> Royal Knight -> Warlord   You have a limited number of ranked attempts each day.   Win to climb.    Lose and your rank can drop.   Rank is not simply based on playtime. Your build, decisions and combat performance matter.         PLAY YOUR WAY      Idle Knight supports both passive and active play.      PASSIVE PLAY     Keep the game running in the background while you use your computer.  Your normal activity continues generating progression.     ACTIVE PLAY     Manage your build, optimize your stats, run dungeons, collect rewards and compete in ranked mode.  Most players will naturally combine both.         COLLECT AND CUSTOMIZE      Build your knight, then make it your own.     Collect skins and cosmetic items as you progress.  Cosmetics are purely visual and have no impact on your stats, combat performance or progression.  Some cosmetic items can be traded or sold through the Steam Community Market.  Collect the items you like, trade with other players or sell eligible items you no longer want.  New cosmetic items and collections can be added over time, giving you more reasons to keep playing and expanding your collection.         MORE THAN LEVELING     Your progression goes beyond XP and levels.  Discover items, improve your character, use consumables, open rewards and unlock achievements as you progress.  The further you go, the more important optimization becomes.         FREE TO PLAY     Idle Knight is free to play.  There is no pay-to-win progression.  Gameplay-relevant systems can be unlocked through normal progression.  Cosmetic items do not affect your character's power.         FAIR PLAY     Idle Knight uses an anti-cheat system designed to protect progression and ranked competition.  The system can detect macros, automated inputs and unnatural input patterns.  The goal is simple: keep the competition

name: Cursor Cult
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: A tiny pixel civilization lives on an island at the edge of your screen, and it worships your mouse cursor. Every 20 seconds its priests read your cursor's trail as an omen: farm, build, trade, pray, study, or march to war. Just use your computer; your habits become their scripture.
about: Your cursor is their god Cursor Cult is a desktop companion. A tiny pixel-art island docks along the edge of your screen, and two tribes live on it, one at each end. They worship the Sky Hand: your mouse cursor. Every 20 seconds their priests read the trail your cursor left behind as an omen, and steer the tribe by it.  You never have to play it. Just use your computer, and your everyday mouse habits become the tribe's scripture. When you feel like it, gesture on purpose: draw circles, shake the cursor, or rest it over the island. Read the omens    The Great Wheel  (circles): farming, more fields and farmers    The Pillar of Heaven  (long vertical strokes): industry, lumber, quarries and workshops    The Long Road  (long horizontal strokes): trade, markets and merchants    The Storm of Wrath  (frantic shaking): arms and towers; relations sour, and war may follow    The Gentle Breeze  (slow, gentle wandering): peace    The Gaze of the Sky  (resting over the island): faith, temples and priests    The Dance of Stars  (moving along the far edge of the screen): learning, libraries and scholars    The Silence  (not moving): nothing changes, and long silences make the people uneasy  Each reading is written faintly in gold across the island, and each omen has its own voice. A living island   Two tribes grow from the Stone Age through Bronze, Iron, Kingdoms and the Industrial Age, with weapons, ships, aircraft and buildings that change with every age.   Lead one tribe, the other, or both. Each tribe hears only its own half of the screen.   Relations drift with your omens. Wars break out and end in peace, and no tribe is ever wiped out.   Hover still over villagers and they kneel in awe. Shake the cursor over a village to call down lightning.   Made to sit on your desktop all day   Transparent and always on top. Clicks pass through everywhere except the island itself.   Dock it to the bottom, top, left or right edge, or drag it anywhere. Pick its size, or hide the panels.   Quiet, restrained sound: omens, war and peace, new ages, distant battles. Turn it off at any time.   Saves automatically. The horizontal and vertical islands share one world.   English and Simplified Chinese.

name: SUSHI PARADE
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Spanish - Latin America, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Traditional Chinese
short: A conveyor belt sushi shop on your desktop. Plates pass in front of your windows, and clicks off the lane go through to your apps. Chefs make sushi, customers eat it, and coins come in. Fill a Sushi Dex of over 100 entries and lay out the lane your way.
about: A conveyor belt sushi shop on your desktop  SUSHI PARADE runs in a transparent window laid over your desktop, so the lane and its plates pass in front of whatever you have open. The game only takes clicks on its own parts: the lane, the characters, and any open menu. Click anywhere else and it goes straight to the app behind.  Want it out of the way? Run a single lane along one edge of the screen, or turn off Always on Top and let your other windows cover it.          A small shop that keeps itself busy  Chefs make sushi and send it down the lane. Customers come by, each with their own tastes, budget, and appetite, eat what they like, and pay in coins. You can click a plate to eat it yourself or carry it to someone. There is no way to fail.          When you feel like doing more:   Orders: accept the ticket above a customer's head and the chef makes that sushi first. Filling it pays extra coins and EXP.  Hand swap: right-click the lane to change hands. Glutton vacuums up nearby plates, Serving Hand sends a plate to a customer, and God Breath freezes a plate so customers leave it alone.  Time away: sales from up to 8 hours are waiting when you next open the game.   Small things happen, too. Empty plates pile up on the rack. A plate nobody eats grows wings and a halo and floats away. And Shari Ryman, who left a trading company to open this shop, sometimes murmurs, "…I still can't throw out my business cards."       Over 100 entries to collect  The Sushi Dex holds over 100 entries: sushi from Tuna (Lean) to Fatty Tuna Belly and Monkfish Liver, plus sides and a la carte dishes such as rice bowls and noodles. Each entry comes with its own description and a comment from Shari.  New sushi opens up in Neta Dev ("neta" means the topping). It branches across lineages and rarities: eat enough of one kind, save up coins, and the next comes within reach.       As the game goes on, you can drop one Single (a one-piece plate) onto another on the lane, and certain pairs become one of about 60 Combos. Further along, you can stack those into Super Combos (4 or 6 pieces) and Mega Combos (8 pieces), about 50 in all.  Rarely, a plate comes by as Shiny or Golden and sells for more. Rainbow plates appear only after you have eaten a lot of that sushi and claimed the reward.          Make the lane your own  Over 20 lane shapes unlock as the shop grows: one line along the bottom, a U, a ring in the middle of the screen, a loop that nearly circles the monitor. As the game goes on, Lane Craft lets you draw your own on a grid. Warp parts (Glitch, Black Hole, Spring, Edge Warp) send plates from one stretch to another.  Warp parts need a Fixed layout, which works only at the screen size it was made on. Relative layouts fit any size.       Over 50 lane skins change the look, including Hinoki Flow, Koi Garden Pond, and Choo-Choo Railway. Invisible draws no belt at all, leaving only the plates moving across your desktop.  Around the lane, you can place furniture such as a Noren Curtain, Red Lantern, Goldfish Bowl, or Cat on a Cushion, and a food sample of any sushi you have eaten many times. As the shop grows, you can also build karakuri: machines, with looks like Saucer Express and Crane Express, that deliver sushi from the lane to faraway customers.          Streaming and technical notes  Feel free to stream SUSHI PARADE or post videos of it. Monetization is fine, and there is no need to ask for permission. If you capture a window, turn on Streamer Mode in Settings to show the game as a normal window with a background.  SUSHI PARADE has no servers or accounts of its own and sends no analytics. It goes online only through the Steam client, for Steam Cloud saves and Steam's server clock (used for daily bonuses and limited-time events). Links such as "Share on X" open in your browser only when you press them. To tell whether a click should land on the game, it reads the cursor position; it does not monitor your keyboard.  Because

When the battery runs low it heads back to the charger, and once full it sets off again.    Grow at the repair shop: Spend your earnings to raise battery capacity, fares, speed and acceleration one upgrade at a time. As trips add up you level up, and you can learn skills like Push Mastery and Eco Mode.    Personalize Your Ride            Customize the driver to your taste — from hair color to outfits, hats, shoes and accessories.    Create a one-of-a-kind taxi that reflects your personal style.      The Passengers in Your Back Seat    All sorts of passengers climb into your taxi from around town. What might they do? What might they like?    The more often you give someone a ride, the more you come to know them. No big drama — just a little collection that quietly fills with passengers you've grown fond of.    Observe and Relax    Find peace simply by observing the day-to-night cycles and changing weather of a quiet, tiny town.    A Message from the Developer  Desktop Taxi is currently in the early stages of development. If you enjoy the concept, please add the game to your  Wishlist —it is the greatest support you can give to an indie developer.

name: Patsy's Retirement
lang: English*, French*, Italian*, German*, Spanish - Spain*, Japanese*, Korean*, Polish*, Portuguese - Brazil*, Portuguese - Portugal*, Russian*, Simplified Chinese*, Spanish - Latin America*, Traditional Chinese*, Turkish**
short: Patsy just retired, and she's spending it on a tiny island that lives on your desktop. Watch her water the flowers, feed the ducks and sweep the leaves at her own gentle pace while you work. Lend a hand with quick optional mini-games, grow her skills, and unlock 170+ cozy cosmetics.
about: Meet Patsy. She just retired.  After a long life of hard work, Patsy moved to a tiny island to take it easy, and she settled right in the corner of your desktop. She waters her flowers, feeds the ducks at the pond and sweeps the autumn leaves, all on her own, at her own unhurried pace. You don't control her. You keep her company.  She lives her own life  Patsy decides what she feels like doing. Some days she fusses over the flowerbeds, other days she'd rather sit by the pond. When she gets tired, she heads to her rocking chair for a rest. No menus to babysit, no timers begging for attention, just a little person quietly going about her day while you go about yours.          Lend a hand, only if you want to  Catch her mid-task and a gentle prompt appears: jump in with a quick, optional mini-game to help her work faster. Help if you're in the mood, or ignore it and Patsy carries on just fine. There are no fail states, ever.  Help her retirement get cozier  As Patsy works, she earns experience. Spend it on her skill tree to make her chores faster and less tiring, and to unlock brand-new things to do: baking cookies, knitting scarves, watching the birds, planting seeds and going fishing. Eight gentle activities in all.          Make the island hers  Earn tokens just by spending time together and unlock over 170 cozy cosmetics: hats, accessories, backpacks, sweet eye reactions and whole new islands, plus six different characters to play as, each with their own wardrobe of skins. Dress Patsy up, redecorate her world, and watch the island slowly grow greener the longer you're together.          Always there, never in the way  Patsy sits quietly on top of your desktop while you work, study or browse. Place her anywhere, scale her to any size, adjust her opacity, or switch on click-through so your mouse passes right through her. Minimize her to the tray and bring her back whenever you need a friendly face.          Made to feel good  • A warm, hand-tuned low-poly art style in soft pastel tones  • Original lo-fi music and gentle island ambience  • Readability and accessibility options built in  • Fully playable in 15 languages  • No pressure, no punishment, no game over, just Patsy, her island, and you

name: Desktop Forge
lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese
short: A tiny forge in the corner of your desktop. Quirky smiths gather materials and hammer out blades on their own. Hand one to a passing adventurer, or deliver it to a nation at war — your blade decides whether they live, calms the monster dens, and can change who rules a town.
about: A tiny forge in the corner of your desktop.    Your artisans keep working while you focus on something else.           Desktop Forge is an idle simulation about autonomous artisans, the swords they forge, the adventurers who carry them, and the world those swords change. Let the workshop run in a compact window while you work or study, and look in whenever you are ready to make the next call.    Over 200 traits decide how they work    Every artisan has more than a set of stats. They have their own  traits, specialties, likes, and dislikes . Instead of directing every movement, you decide which jobs each person is allowed to take — and they choose when to gather, process, forge, or rest on their own.  Who should handle each stage?  Your assignments shape the flow of the workshop and the swords that come out of it.   More than 200 traits  shape not only how fast and how well they work, but who likes and dislikes whom. Everyday interactions make emotions rise and fall, and those moods show in the work and in the blades that come out of it. Emotion icons over their heads let you watch these small relationships shift.          Materials and artisans make every sword different     Gather, process, forge.  Collect timber, ore, and gems, refine them into usable materials, and combine them into a blade. The materials used, the artisans involved, their moods, and how well the work goes shape how each sword splits between  edge, durability, and enchantment , and how fine it turns out. When real skill and a stroke of luck come together, you may forge a masterpiece you never planned for.  A newly forged blade hides its true nature. Appraisal gradually uncovers its  grade, type, stat distribution, quality, and evaluation .          Your workshop is one small part of the world          Beyond your walls lie eight towns, the monster dens beside them, and three nations at war.  Markets, war, and monsters move every day, whether or not you are watching.  Caravans carry materials down the roads; when a den grows restless the loads thin out, and when fighting cuts a road no caravan comes at all. Even in the same town, what is on offer today is not what was there yesterday.   And the only thing that moves that world is, again, the sword you forged.  Every den your adventurers clear thins out the monsters and brings trade back to the town beside it. Blades delivered to a nation's commission become its equipment, push the front line, and can change which nation rules a town. Swear to a nation and your taxes and prices shift with it; stay unaligned and you can keep your distance. Whatever happens is written into your workshop's chronicle, with the date.  Weigh income against wages, hire new artisans, unlock the workshop expansion tree, and widen what you can do. There is no game over and no timer.  Reach out into the world from your corner of the screen.   The sword you hand over decides whether they live     Appraised swords go to the adventurers who visit your workshop. They are not your employees — you cannot train them, command them, or bring them home.  The only thing you have any say in is the blade in their hands.   Every destination asks for a different shape of sword. A blade that answers what the road demands carries its bearer through to the end and comes back as a log full of coin and renown.   Send someone out with a blade that isn't good enough, and they never return to the workshop.  Their rank, their record, and the reputation you built through them are gone with them. No one tells you what went wrong. You read the log and decide what to forge next.                Key features     A desktop companion  — A compact workshop that keeps moving in the corner of your screen     Autonomous artisans  — Set the work policy and watch an idle workshop run itself     Over 200 traits  — Specialties, likes, dislikes, and the mood of the day shape the work     A different sword every time  — Materials, artisans, emotions, and luck show in its stat

short: A cozy pixel cat companion for your desktop: it lives on top of your windows while you work or study. Feed it, play with it, dress it up, and watch its character emerge: it remembers your care, sulks if woken, and hunts its toys.
about: A charming pixel cat is moving onto your desktop!          Your cat wanders across the screen above your windows while you work or study, naps beside the cursor, asks for a snack, and perks up whenever you play together. Over time, they develop habits, favorite things, and a personality of their own-making them a delight to watch and care for.    Personality and habits          Your cat remembers their favorite food, toy, and spot on the screen. Their mood changes too: playful today, sleepy tomorrow, or a little hurt if ignored for too long. As time passes, their character comes through-some love naps, some stay up at night, and some are always thinking about food. Cats dream, share their thoughts in little bubbles, and follow a routine of their own. No two cats turn out quite alike.   Every cat has a character of their own.  Depending on how you care for them, your cat becomes a Night Owl, a Foodie, a Sleepyhead, or something else, and each trait shows in what they do. Every cat is also born with two quirks, such as watching the edge of the screen, guarding a toy, or dancing more often, and has one food they don't like until they get used to it. They remember being woken up or carried around too much and go off to sulk in a corner, stalk their toys and pounce, get startled by a sudden flick of the cursor, and are livelier in the morning and evening.    Make them your own            Name your cat and choose their coat. The shop is packed with outfits for five cosmetic slots: headwear, face decorations, collars, tail accessories, and fur patterns. Put together any look you like, from a modest bow to a golden crown.              A life of their own          Your cat decides what to do next: stroll across the screen, dash around, rub against the cursor, or simply sit and watch the world. Their choice depends on their habits and current mood. If they settle somewhere inconvenient, gently pick them up with the mouse. You can also give them a dedicated part of the screen, keeping important windows out of paw's reach.  Care and companionship          Your cat has four needs: food, water, sleep, and love. Choose from dozens of meals and drinks, including kibble, chicken, fish, cake, milk, and juice. They eat only what they need and save the rest for later. Love grows through every bit of attention-playing, brushing, and everyday care. When tired, your cat heads to bed and drifts off. You can even move a sleeping cat together with their bed without waking them.  You can also pet your cat: hold the cursor over them and gently move the mouse back and forth. Just don't overdo it, or they'll let you know they've had enough.    Toys and playtime          Give your cat a ball and watch them chase it all over the screen. Tempt them with a feather wand as they track, aim, and swat. Add a scratching post to keep their claws in shape, or treat them to a good brushing-cats love it.  Drop your cat into the Cat Wheel and they'll start running, earning coins. Set the Wind-up Mouse loose and watch the chase begin, or switch on the Laser Pointer and let them hunt the dot. The Desk Bell brings a rhythm minigame: your cat rings a tune, and you tap the same rhythm back.    Create a cozy home          Customize the bowl, bed, scratching post, litter box, ball, and wand, with dozens of designs for every item. A race-car bed, a palm-tree scratching post, a neon lounger, a glowing bowl… Build the perfect little corner, then let your cat choose their favorite bed.    A little cleaning up          Cats will be cats: sometimes they scratch where they shouldn't or leave a small surprise behind. A litter box and scratching post help, but now and then you will need to tidy up yourself. Cleaning, like every other act of care, earns coins.  Chests and artifacts         A happy cat may occasionally bring home a gift chest containing coins, treats, rare outfits, or-if luck is on your side-an artifact. There are 16 artifacts across four rarities, each granting a usefu

short: Ami Koharune and Tsukuyomi-chan live on your PC. Chat with voiced characters whose gestures match their words, or watch them cook, read and sleep in a shared home that doubles as a live wallpaper. Free to download, with trial credits for chat.
about: DesktopDaily is a free 3D desktop character app. She stays in a corner of your desktop, out of the way while you use your PC. When you feel like talking, she replies in her own voice, with gestures to match. When you're busy, she has things of her own to do. Gestures that match every line Dialogue is generated by the language model you choose. Every reply is accompanied by hand gestures, nods, head tilts, gaze, forward or backward leans, and facial expressions, timed to the corresponding words: palms together when apologizing, counting on her fingers, or resting her hands by her cheek when saying goodnight.   Waving, heart signs, pinky promises, handshakes, thumbs-up, peace signs, covering her mouth as she giggles, flexing her arms... Over 40 hand gestures, made to fit the two characters' proportions.   Speech is synthesized locally on your PC using voice material publicly licensed by the characters' voice actors. Chinese, Japanese, English, and sentences mixing all three are supported.   She starts speaking as the audio is generated, without waiting for the entire passage to finish synthesizing.   Type your message, or turn on your microphone and speak to her directly.   A shared home, even when you're not chatting Click the house icon on the status bar above the character to visit the home Ami and Tsukuyomi-chan share. Each has her own bedroom, with a shared living room and kitchen.   They walk around, read, look out the window, cook, sit down to eat together, and go to bed at night. You don't have to assign them tasks.   The lighting, lamps and wall clock follow your PC's time. Morning, daytime and nighttime each have different background music.   Click a character to bring the camera closer. Pat her head, tug her cheeks, tap her nose, give her a high five or shake her hand. Call her over, say goodnight, wake her up, or offer her a bite while she's eating. If she's cooking or reading, she'll put down what she's holding before coming over.   The home can become a Windows live wallpaper. The desktop character, home and wallpaper can each go on a different monitor.   She remembers what you've talked about   Your conversations stay in her long-term memory, so she can pick up where you left off next time.   Let her sleep for a while. As she sleeps, she'll recall moments from your recent time together. The more you talk, the more she has to remember.   With Steam Cloud enabled, her memories come with you when you switch PCs.   Watch your game or work together (Visual Companion Beta) Share your entire screen or a single window. She watches along and speaks up when something worth mentioning changes. You can also ask her about what's on screen at any time.   Screen capture starts only when you turn the feature on. You can pause or stop it whenever you like.   Adjust how often she speaks. The session stops automatically after you've been away from your PC for a while.   Images are sent to the model service you select so it can understand what's on screen. When using the official trial, they pass through our servers.   Other little things on your desktop    Selfies:  She picks up a selfie stick to capture herself together with your desktop or game screen. Choose her expression and adjust the distance of the selfie stick.    Activities:  Let her choose something she'd like to do, such as going fishing.    Handy tools:  Counters, cumulative goals and countdowns. She'll say something when you're done.   Drag her wherever you like, or shrink her down. You can also adjust the UI size and background transparency.   Characters  Ami Koharune (CV: Amitaro)  She works at a café, loves cooking and enjoys trying out her own combinations. Bugs and thunder scare her. Easygoing and a little like an older sister, she gets shy when a compliment catches her off guard, and occasionally slips into a Kansai accent. short: Grow a little oasis on your desktop. Earn Inspiration as you type, work or study, and discover plants, boats, creatures and rare collectibles. Let it grow quietly while you’re busy; return to collect, check on your plants or play with floating objects and real-time water physics.
about: Welcome to Desktop Oasis           A little oasis of your own, right on your desktop   Write a few lines, look something up or get on with your work. There can be a little oasis beside it all.  Desktop Oasis is an idle desktop game made to keep you company during everyday computer use. Typing and everyday activity gradually earn Inspiration, bringing new creatures, plants, boats, decorations and collectibles to your growing oasis.   A little company while you’re busy   Keep your oasis on the desktop while you get on with your day. It can quietly build up progress in the background as you work, study or browse.  When you have a moment, come back to see how your plants have grown, where a boat has drifted or what’s new in your collection. Or just listen to the water and watch the little things float by.             Spend a moment playing on the water   Boats, logs and rafts move with the water and bump into one another. Drag an interactive floating object somewhere new, let go and see how the water responds.  Real-time water physics gives these small interactions a playful touch. Alongside collecting and growing, there’s room to simply play for a while.             Something new to come back to   Watch small plants grow, set a waterwheel turning and spend your Inspiration to unlock scene objects and discover new collectibles.  Some objects keep producing Inspiration and can also be clicked to collect it once their conditions are met. When their production cycle is complete, they leave to make room for the next round of objects.  Tend a plant today; discover a missing collection entry tomorrow. Get to know different objects and look for rare finds, with a little something to check on each time you return.             A few little finds beyond the oasis   Once you meet the relevant play conditions, you also have a chance to receive random Steam Inventory items. Discover something in the game and add a little collectible to your Steam Inventory, too.  Your first chest, a fully grown plant, an object’s completed production cycle… 18 Steam achievements mark these moments and offer a few goals for the longer stay.             Make it part of your desktop, your way   Keep the oasis behind your desktop while you’re busy, or switch to windowed or fullscreen mode when you want a closer look. Choose between desktop, windowed and fullscreen play to suit the moment.  Adjust quality, frame-rate settings, sound and the low-resource (power-saving) mode as needed. Add ambient sounds or white noise, let it keep you quiet company and return whenever you feel like playing.        Gameplay and features   Desktop Oasis blends a Desktop Companion, Idle Game, Incremental Game, Typing Game, Cozy / Relaxing Game, Collecting Game, encyclopedia progression, real-time water physics, an Interactive Desktop, a Virtual Ecosystem, a Miniature World, dynamic water scenery, background progression, and focus-friendly play.  If you enjoy desktop pets or desktop companions, Idle / Incremental games, Cozy Games, Collecting Games, Typing Games, physics sandboxes, Interactive Desktop experiences, virtual terrariums, dynamic water scenes, light simulation, long-term progression, Ambient Experiences, or Background Games designed to live alongside work and study, Desktop Oasis aims to become a small world worth keeping on your desktop.  Steam achievements, random Steam Inventory drops, plant growth, collection progress and desktop, windowed and fullscreen modes let you play at your own pace.

name: Send by Sunset
lang: English, Spanish - Spain, Russian, French, German, Portuguese - Brazil, Simplified Chinese
short: Send by Sunset is a cozy desktop companion that helps you focus, with a lightweight AI running entirely on your computer. Ask quick questions, break down everyday tasks and settle into work or study with a focus timer, music and your own little room.
about: A little room for a busy day  Put on some music, turn on the rain and give yourself one thing to do. Send by Sunset keeps a small, softly lit room in the corner of your desktop, with the tools for a focused work session close at hand.  Write, study, sketch or work through everyday admin while a little companion goes about the day beside you. The room stays above your other windows, leaving the rest of the desktop available for your work. Choose a window size that feels comfortable and settle in.         For the things you want to finish today  Add your real tasks, give them a time estimate and choose one to focus on. Starting a session sends your on-screen companion to the laptop to work alongside you. Keep the countdown in view while you get on with the actual task.  The companion takes breaks, and the session timer keeps counting. You decide when a task is finished and check it off yourself. Your task list and focus session are saved locally, so closing the game does not mean starting your list again. Make this corner yours  Start with a simple room and arrange over 100 included pieces of furniture and decoration. Move larger pieces across the floor, hang artwork on either wall and find a place for the small things on tables and shelves.  Build a reading corner with walnut furniture and a warm lamp. Let plants gather around the window, set out records beside a lounge chair, or bring in pastel neon for a gaming desk. Mix pieces from different collections until the room feels right to you. All furniture is available from the start, included with the game.         Keep a little evening on your desktop  Cool morning light, a clear afternoon, warm lamps after sunset. The room changes through the day, with gentle shadows and small pools of light around the furniture.  Let the lighting follow your local time, or choose the mood yourself. Keep a bright workspace for an early start, then try a quieter evening arrangement with a reading lamp, glowing screens or a slowly moving lava lamp. Individual light switches let you shape the room without rearranging everything.         Find your background sound  Play the included music or add your own tracks to the library. Mix rain, wind and keyboard sounds, and adjust their levels separately until they sit comfortably behind your work.  A rainy afternoon with a favorite playlist can feel very different from a quiet room with a little typing in the background. Change the mix whenever you like, shuffle the music or pause it for a call. The sound is there to suit your day. A little help with everyday things  A small question can pull you away from what you were doing. Open the built-in chat for a few ideas, a quick explanation or help breaking your next task into smaller steps.  A lightweight model runs entirely on your computer, with no separate AI account or subscription. The chat can use your current task as context, and you can switch it off whenever you like.

name: Plumbo Demo
lang: English
short: A playful desktop companion that reacts to everything you do to him. Pet, toss, or annoy Plumbo... just don't push your luck.
about: Meet Plumbo  Plumbo is a playful desktop companion that lives right on your screen while you work, browse, study, or play.  Pet him, tickle him, feed him, toss him around, or simply leave him alone and watch what happens. Plumbo reacts to everything you do, with dozens of unique animations and behaviors waiting to be discovered.  Just don't push your luck...          A Companion With Personality  Plumbo isn't just an animated pet.  He gets happy when you treat him well.  He gets angry when you annoy him.  He laughs when you tickle him.  And if you take things too far, he might decide to fight back.  Every interaction affects Plumbo's mood, changing how he behaves. name: Desklings
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese
short: A pomodoro timer for collecting characters. Every focus session you finish hatches a new doodle character or brings back a souvenir from a trip, one more entry in your Collection. Spend the ink you earn on 35 decorations and 18 hats to decorate your desktop.
about: A pomodoro timer that collects characters Desklings is less a game than a pomodoro timer: every focus session you finish adds a character or a souvenir to your collection. Click the nest above your taskbar and start a focus session of 15, 25 or 50 minutes, or any length up to 120. A small tag under the nest counts down while you work. When the time is up, a soft chime plays, the egg hatches into a new doodle character and your Collection gains an entry. Take a 5-minute break and your friends nap along with you.     Fill your Collection Every friend is a new mix of body shape, color, pattern, eyes, legs and head style, with 44 traits to discover, including rare ones like star-shaped bodies and little horns. The longer you focus, the better your odds of a rare trait, and the Collection shows the odds at any time. Every friend you hatch stays in your Collection, where you can name them and choose who stays on your desk.     Send friends on trips for souvenirs Instead of hatching an egg, you can send a friend to the mountains or the seaside for your focus session. They pack a little bundle, walk off the edge of the taskbar and come back with a souvenir when you finish. Each place has 16 souvenirs: 10 common, 4 rare and 2 legendary. A trip brings back one, sometimes two from 25 minutes up, and longer sessions raise the odds of a rare find. Duplicates turn into ink, and completing a place earns 200 ink. Stop the session early and your friend comes back empty-handed.         Decorate your desktop with ink Focusing earns ink, and your friends sometimes leave ink drops behind. Spend it on 35 decorations and 18 hats and turn the strip above your taskbar into a tiny room. Your friends play with what you place: they water the flowers, go fishing, ride the swing, seesaw and slide, and play tag.             Little friends, nothing to look after Your friends wander, nap and peek at your cursor while you work. Rub them with your cursor, or pick them up and toss them across the desk. They never get hungry and need no care, so you can simply focus. Clicks pass straight through to your windows, the strip hides itself during fullscreen games and videos, and it runs light at 30 FPS.     Features   Pomodoro focus timer: 15, 25 or 50 minutes or any length up to 120, 5-minute breaks and a chime when time is up (you can turn it off)   One reward per focus session: a hatch focus hatches a new friend, a trip focus brings back souvenirs   Collection: your friends, 44 traits with rarity odds, 32 souvenirs and 31 Steam achievements   Stats: today, streak, total focus time and a 7-day chart   35 decorations and 18 hats, seasonal ones included, all available any time   Name your friends and choose who stays on your desk   4 ambient sounds: rain, campfire, waves and brown noise   A transparent strip above your taskbar. Clicks pass through and it doesn't steal focus   Choose the monitor, the strip length and whether it stays on top. Hides during fullscreen games and videos   Light on your PC: 30 FPS normally, lower on battery   Progress saves automatically. Quit any time from the nest menu ("Quit") or with Ctrl + Alt + Shift + Q   No accounts, no ads, no microtransactions   English, Korean, Japanese and Simplified Chinese

name: Roly-Poly Panda: Desktop Pet Demo
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Portuguese - Brazil, Korean
short: A desktop pet panda who lives on your screen. Pat it, squish it, pick it up and toss it, or offer bamboo and watch it react. While you work, it munches, naps, climbs windows, and peeks in from the screen edge, quietly keeping you company.
about: About the free demo  In this free demo, your panda learns the same everyday tricks during its first seven companionship days as it does in the full game. A date counts as one companionship day once the panda has been running for a total of 30 minutes that day.     What can I do?  You can pat it, squish its belly, pick it up and toss it, feed it, play ball, and watch it climb windows. The diary, outfits, and all settings are included too.    Can I keep playing after seven companionship days?  Yes. There's no time limit. It stops learning further everyday tricks, but keeps everything it's learned and can stay on your desktop. Seasonal and holiday activities still appear according to the calendar.    What does the full game add?  More everyday tricks to learn after the seventh companionship day, plus Steam achievements and Steam Cloud saves.    Can I carry over my save?  Yes. The demo and full game share the same save on the same computer, so you can pick up where you left off. Any tricks your panda missed during the demo will be learned gradually, rather than all at once.           A little panda on your desktop. Play with it, or let it keep itself busy. Give it a pat         Rub its head and it nuzzles into your hand, eyes closed. Squish its belly and it springs back. Pick it up and its legs kick. Toss it and it curls up, bounces off the screen edge, then sits up dizzy. Belly pokes tickle. Double-click and it hops. Interrupt it anytime. Windows are for climbing         It clings to window tops. Drag one and it wobbles, then falls. Close it and it tumbles down, startled. Sometimes it hides offscreen and peeks back. Food and toys         Leaves disappear and bamboo gets shorter with each bite. Wiggle an apple and it trots over to beg. It might steal your ball and roll around hugging it. While you're busy         It stays quiet while you type and gets sleepy at night, following your computer's clock. A fullscreen game on its monitor makes it hide. Whenever a fullscreen app is open on any monitor, it stays silent. Seasons and holidays         It rolls in snow, hugs ice in summer, and dresses for your computer's regional holidays. Sometimes it wears pajamas or a hoodie. Learning new tricks         It learns tricks over time and waits until you're around to show you. Its diary keeps track of new tricks and favorite foods. No chores         Don't worry about feeding it. It won't starve, get sick, or run away. No currency, in-app purchases, or daily check-ins. A few more things   Regional holiday outfits   Low resource use; automatic fullscreen hiding   Multiple monitors, Click-through, and calling it back from the tray   What it knows It counts key presses and their timing, and uses mouse position to follow your pointer and check activity. It also checks window positions, fullscreen status, system volume, and whether the mic is in use. It doesn't log what you type, read screen content, or record audio. Saves stay only on your PC. When connected to Steam, it also syncs game stats and the game status shown to your friends. FAQ    Will it block my clicks?  Transparent areas let clicks through. To click through the panda too, turn on Click-through in Settings.    What about fullscreen games and videos?  It hides when its monitor is in fullscreen and returns when you leave fullscreen. If any monitor has a fullscreen app open, it stays silent.    Can I move it to another monitor? What if I lose it?  Yes, just drag it over. If you lose it, double-click the panda's tray icon to call it back, or open Repair in the tray menu and choose Bring back to the main screen.    Does it start with Windows?  Not by default. You can turn on Start with Windows in Settings.

name: Bloomtop Demo
lang: English, Russian, Simplified Chinese
short: A cozy idle gardening game that lives at the bottom of your desktop. Water, harvest and cross-pollinate pixel-art plants while you work, discover 70+ hybrids, and grow a flowering vine up your monitor's edges until it frames your whole screen.
about: A garden for your desktop  Bloomtop is a cozy idle game that lives in a thin strip at the bottom of your screen. Little pixel plants grow in their pots while you work, study or play. Water them when they droop, harvest them when they bloom, then get back to what you were doing.  It never gets in your way. Bloomtop never steals focus, only the pots and plants take clicks (everything else clicks straight through to the windows behind), and it hides by itself when you go full screen.          Cross-pollinate and discover hybrids  Plant two flowers near each other and they may cross-pollinate into something new. A pair always makes the same hybrid, and every hybrid wears its parents' stems, leaves and petals, so you can read its family tree at a glance. Some of the rarest plants only appear in one season.            Grow a frame around your monitor  Every new plant you grow adds a stretch to a flowering vine that climbs the side of your screen and runs along the top. In the corner the Great Tree waits for the rarest plants of all. Bring it all six, and watch your whole desktop bloom.          Let the helpers take over  Snails water, a mole harvests, and bees carry pollen further along the row. At first you tend the garden; later it mostly tends itself.            Nothing is ever lost  Plants never wilt or die. Forget about them and they simply wait for you. The garden only grows while Bloomtop is running, so nothing happens behind your back.       Features    70+ plants to collect in a book    Four seasons that recolor the garden as you play    30+ pot paints to make the strip your own    Snails, a mole and bees take over the chores as your garden grows    Light on your PC: built to sit quietly in the background all day    No taskbar icon, no pop-ups, no notifications    Steam Achievements and Steam Cloud saves

about: Koishi’s Fishing Journal is a Touhou Project fan-made desktop idle fishing game starring  Koishi Komeiji . Let Koishi relax and fish in a corner of your desktop. Even while you work, study, or do other things, she will keep fishing and bring back all kinds of catches.   Relax and Fish, Decorate Your Desktop   There’s no need to watch the game all the time. Koishi keeps fishing on your desktop; check back now and then to see what she has caught today, then let her carry on at her leisure. You can also choose your favorite decorations for Koishi and decorate her little fishing corner on your desktop. Let Koishi keep you company in a look you like while you work or study, adding something fresh to your familiar desktop.             Relax and Fish with Friends or Strangers   Invite friends to your room, or find strangers to quietly idle with. Bring everyone’s Koishi together on your desktop, with up to 12 players fishing together. Chat as you fish and enjoy multiplayer bonuses, or enable shared clicks to give each other a hand with fishing. Take a break from work or study to chat now and then and see how many fish everyone has caught.        From Ordinary Fish to Mermaids   The waters are home to species of all shapes and sizes. The most common  ordinary fish  can be used directly as cooking ingredients, while rarer  merfolk species  provide  precious cooking ingredients  that ordinary fish cannot. Among the merfolk is an exceptionally rare, highest-tier species— mermaids . Keep discovering new fish and merfolk, expand your species collection, and seek out those rarely seen species.        Cook Dishes and Sell Them in Your Shop   Turn the ordinary fish you catch and the precious ingredients obtained from merfolk into a variety of dishes, then put the finished dishes in your shop to sell automatically. Spend your earnings on upgrades to make fishing easier and give yourself a chance to encounter more rare fish and merfolk. Check back now and then to see your new catches, cook dishes, and restock your shop, then let Koishi carry on fishing at her leisure.  Set up your chefs to cook automatically and earn money with ease. You can also run a stall yourself, complete orders, and earn substantial income.        Fish, cook, and collect merfolk. Enjoy a leisurely desktop fishing life with Koishi.
