name: Cart Panic! OS - E-Commerce Tycoon
lang: English, Italian, Spanish - Spain, Spanish - Latin America, Japanese, Russian
short: Run an online store inside a chaotic operating system. Hackers attack, viruses pop up, customers rage, and a card game tempts your profits.
about: Cart Panic! OS  is not just a tycoon game. It's a fully functional operating system where you run an online store while hackers attack you, viruses pop up, customers rage in chat, and a high-stakes card game tempts you to gamble your profits away.  You start with $50, an ugly desktop, and your first debt. Your store has zero reviews. Your first supplier is already late. Then everything happens at once. Your Desktop, Your Business This isn't a menu-based tycoon. Every system runs through apps on your desktop. Drag windows, multitask between crises, and watch your taskbar fill up as chaos escalates.     19 functional apps  - Dashboard, Analytics, Marketing, Finance, Employees, Hacking Terminal, Antivirus, MetaStack card game, and more    Real window management  - Minimize, resize, stack, and juggle multiple windows as orders pile up    Persistent threats  - Viruses spawn randomly, slow your system, corrupt data, and demand ransom   Run Your Store Build your e-commerce business from scratch. Design your storefront, negotiate with suppliers, fulfill orders, and survive the constant pressure of unhappy customers.     Website Studio  - Design your store with layouts, themes, colors and fonts. Your design choices affect conversion rates    Supply Hub  - Manage inventory, browse suppliers, negotiate prices and delivery times. Cheap suppliers create defects    Customer Chat  - Answer questions, handle complaints, process refunds. One wrong reply can tank your reputation    Marketing Campaigns  - Launch ads, track ROI, and watch your budget burn as algorithms change   HackOS Terminal A full hacking simulator built into the game. Open the terminal, type real commands, and attack targets for massive payouts. Or defend against incoming threats.     Functional CLI  - Navigate directories, run commands, autocomplete, command history    5 hacking minigames  - Password cracking, firewall defense, encryption races, network mazes, packet sniffing    Multiple targets  - From easy marks to extreme difficulty, with risk and reward to match    Attack & defend  - Launch operations or protect your own systems from incoming breaches   MetaStack: Wager Ops A Balatro-inspired roguelike card game hidden inside your desktop. Play poker hands, build combos, collect patches and plugins, and bet real in-game money against escalating contracts.     Poker roguelike  - Play hands from High Card to Five of a Kind, draft upgrades between rounds    Real stakes  - Wager your actual profits. Win big or lose everything    Hype system  - Build multipliers with consecutive wins, up to 10x    4 difficulty tiers  - Safe, Medium, High, Extreme. Payouts scale from 1x to 10x    Overclock mechanic  - Risk instant multipliers with increasing danger   Manage Everything Else    Employees  - Hire staff, train skills, manage salaries, fire underperformers    Finance  - Track cash flow, take loans, pay taxes, avoid bankruptcy    Investments  - Long-term portfolios or arcade-style day trading with stop-loss and take-profit    Analytics  - Sales funnels, customer satisfaction, top products, performance over time    Antivirus  - Scan threats, quarantine malware, enable real-time protection    100+ upgrades  - Eight upgrade branches: Storefront, Logistics, Payments, Marketing, Infrastructure, Expansion, Hacking, Security   Chaos is the Core There is no pause button for the pressure. Customers don't wait. Viruses don't care about your cash flow. Your best employee might quit while you're mid-hack and a refund storm is brewing in chat.  Every session is different. Every decision has trade-offs. Every system affects every other system.  Build your empire. Or watch it crash.

name: DeskForge - Sport Dial Pack
lang: English, French, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Korean, German, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese
short: Five sport chronograph dials for DeskForge's desktop clock — carbon weave, forged carbon, skeleton steel, three-eye layouts and tachymeter rings. A second hand that sweeps instead of ticking, 85 to 1024 px, adjustable transparency, and a carousel that rotates your favourites. Requires DeskForge.
about: A watch that measures how fast, not just what time  A chronograph was never only about telling the time. It was built to time a lap, a pit stop, a straight taken flat out — which is why the dial is crowded, the contrast is loud and the whole thing reads in one glance. This pack puts five of them on your desktop, keeping real time behind everything you have open, so the corner of the screen you keep glancing at finally has some speed in it.           Five sport faces     Contend · Carbon Blazing Red  — carbon dial with black-and-red three-eye chrono and tachymeter ring     Gallop · Carbon Electric Blue  — blue carbon dial, three-eye chrono     Swift Feather · Onyx Neon Green  — black case with neon-green three-eye     Rift · Forged-Carbon Emerald  — forged-carbon dial, green-ringed panda-eye layout     Heart of Gears · Skeleton Steel-Blue  — steel case, skeleton tourbillon chrono, steel-blue sub-dial      How it lives on the desktop     The second hand sweeps.  It glides the way a mechanical movement does, instead of ticking once a second.     Any size you like.  Scale it freely, from a small watch in the corner to something that fills half the desktop. The artwork is drawn at high resolution, so it stays sharp all the way up.     Transparency from 30% to fully solid.  Sink it into the wallpaper or let it stand out.     It sits at the very back.  No taskbar entry, no Alt-Tab clutter, and clicking it never steals focus from whatever you are typing in. Works across multiple monitors.     Very light on resources  — it runs all day and you hardly notice it. And it measures itself: the tray menu shows the CPU and memory it is using at this moment, so you do not have to take our word for it.      Or let them take turns  Pick the faces you actually like and the clock rotates through them on its own — anywhere from once a minute to once every 24 hours, half an hour by default, in order or shuffled. It only ever draws from faces you already own, so the rotation is your collection rather than a catalogue of things you cannot have.    Then change the strap  Nothing changes a sport chronograph faster than what it is mounted on. The separate Watch Strap Pack adds 16 straps across leather, steel bracelet, rubber and NATO nylon, laid flat under the dial or wrapped around it in 3D, with how much strap shows adjustable from 20% up to fully extended. Rubber under carbon is the obvious move; a steel bracelet under the skeleton tourbillon is the one that changes the whole watch.    Other faces, other packs     Dress Dial Pack  — 5 quiet formal faces for when the desktop should just look expensive.     Pilot Dial Pack  — 5 cockpit-legible faces built around oversized numerals.     Diver Dial Pack  — 5 tool-watch faces made to be read in dark water.     Vintage Dial Pack  — 8 pocket watches, lids and chains included.     Tomato Clock and Advanced Time Tools  — a Pomodoro that gets eaten as you focus, plus timer, countdown, stopwatch, alarm and a 20-zone world clock.      What you need  This is a watch-face pack for DeskForge and needs the base app. DeskForge turns a cluttered Windows desktop into somewhere you actually run your day from: drawers that hold your icons and folders, real folders opened right on the wallpaper, and live widgets like this clock.    Windows 10 (version 1903 or later) and Windows 11    Correct scaling at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250%, 300% and 400% DPI    Works across multiple monitors    Interface in English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Russian, Portuguese (Brazil), Portuguese (Portugal), German, Turkish, Thai and Vietnamese    Stored locally in SQLite — no account, no network needed    One-time purchase, no subscription

name: SYSADMIN Hell Demo
lang: English**
short: You're the sole sysadmin for a company scaling from 10 to 100,000 employees. Everything breaks. Everything. Automate your way out of ticket hell or watch it all burn.
about: Welcome to your new job. You're already behind.    You are the only IT person at Pinnacle Synergy Group. There's a queue. It's already full. Users are panicking, Management is angry, and the printer is hostile. Then the company starts to grow.            Grow it. Buy a company. Regret it.  At 12,000 employees, Management buys Halcyon Data Solutions, and their IT becomes yours: a fax machine that is also the email server, forty shared drives called NEW, and a sysadmin who never left. Integrate them in three days, or the board brings in consultants and sends you the bill.            Mine HellCoin on the company servers  The last sysadmin left a crypto miner running in a cupboard in the server room. From your first morning it's yours:    Buy rigs, faster GPUs and liquid cooling, and watch the coins pile up    The price wanders, and jumps or crashes on the headlines    Sell into the IT budget (Finance calls it "cost savings")    The rigs cook the servers and make Compliance curious. Take Compliance to lunch. Switch off before Audit Day. Keep a cold wallet              The Board has three slides  Every few days the Board makes you pick a policy that lasts the rest of your career: Hustle culture, Cloud first, AI-first strategy, Run IT as a profit centre... Every one is a trade, and no two careers end up the same.            Get up from your desk  Some problems can't be fixed from a chair. Walk the office: open-plan floors, a server room that hums, a supply cupboard, and a lift that doesn't stop at 4.     Fix it in person:  trace the right cable, pull a paper jam out the way it went in, find the empty toner, change a light tube without losing your eyebrows     Build PCs at the workbench  for new starters, to their spec and Finance's budget     Run the server room:  amber drive lights, loose cables, fans full of dust              Read the ticket. Fix the problem. Don't make it worse.  Every ticket is a small puzzle, and the answer is usually in the text if you read it properly. Pick the right quick fix and it's gone. Pick the wrong one and it grows.    170+ hand-written tickets that get stranger as the company grows, plus your own: write tickets for your office, or subscribe to packs on the Steam Workshop    Rush hours, SLAs, escalations from executives, and a Chaos meter that sets off incidents when the backlog gets away from you    Hit rock bottom and HR puts you on a Performance Improvement Plan. Meet it, or clear your desk              A whole desktop from 1998  The game is a working late-90s desktop: drag windows, minimise them to the taskbar, live inside HellDesk, HellMail Express, Server Manager and Add/Remove Automation. Automate everything (13 automations, every one fails in its own way), keep it serviced, hire junior admins with real quirks, and watch them burn out.           Or do it all from the command line  The HellDOS Prompt runs the whole job by typing: QUEUE, FIX 12 2, REBOOT MAIL-01, HLC SELL. It also knows a few things it shouldn't. Try PING FLOOR4.           Every day is different    Patch Tuesday, Audit Day, Board Visit, Heatwave, Full Moon, and seasonal days on their real dates    Branching major incidents: ransomware, a reply-all storm that becomes self-aware, a printer hostage situation    A company of the week, the same twist for everyone: a hospital, a law firm, a crypto startup...              Something is wrong with this company  Tickets arrive from nobody. The printer has started writing letters. There's a server nobody installed, warm to the touch. The lift has a button for 4. It has never stopped there. Halcyon's building has a floor 4 too, and their sysadmin knows where the keys are.    Lots to come back for    Multiple endings, and one that's well hidden; an endless mode with milestones and a leaderboard    Three difficulties, contract clauses, and backgrounds that change how a career starts    HellDesk University: permanent perks that carry from career to career    The Daily Shift: the same

name: ECHO
lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian
short: Make your local music your own: organize albums, enjoy immersive lyrics and customize ECHO with Workshop skins, visuals and plugins. Keep controls close with mini players and quick search. Pro is optional for advanced audio and device connections. Bring your own music.
about: Your music, your own little world  ECHO is a desktop player built around  your local music . Deep customization is its defining feature, so there can be a little to learn. If you get stuck, feel free to ask our community! Just remember:  we do not provide a music streaming service .  From playing a favorite album to choosing themes and lyric scenes or adjusting the sound for your headphones and speakers, ECHO brings these experiences into one music space. Simply press play, or explore and make ECHO your own.   ECHO is still in Early Access   Features, interface, performance and device compatibility are still being refined. You may encounter bugs or unfinished experiences. We will keep improving ECHO through updates and use your feedback to guide development. Thank you for supporting us during Early Access. Suggestions are always welcome in our community.   We warmly encourage you to join our community!   Library organization, musical connections and local discovery  From a single album to years of collecting, browse by track, album, artist, genre or folder, and explore the connections within your collection.     Find your next track in your collection:  Local recommendations use musical relationships and listening history to suggest related tracks and rediscover old favorites you have not played in a while.     Organize your library in detail:  Adjust album and artist assignments, merge artist aliases, group different editions of an album, and review duplicates and quality issues.     Bring your formats together:  Play FLAC, WAV, MP3, AAC, ALAC, OGG, Opus and APE, along with CUE tracks and DSD files.    Scanning and automatic analysis only read original media. Results stay in the library or cache; writing tags or embedding artwork and lyrics requires an explicit action from you.  Give every song its own visual stage  Customize the lyrics page so text and effects accompany your music. Expand it further through the Workshop.     Different lyric stages:  Explore panoramic, blended-cover and record-player layouts, with animated backgrounds such as particle formations, particle seas, flip-tile walls and cover ridges.     Lyrics that look the way you want:  Customize both desktop lyrics and the lyrics page, choosing the appearance yourself.     Bring lyrics to your stream:  Use lyrics in an OBS browser source for your own livestreams and recordings.    Keep music and controls within reach     Global quick search:  Open a separate small window with a shortcut, search tracks, artists or albums, browse the queue and playlists, and choose with the arrow keys and Enter.     Controls for your setup:  Use the mini player, desktop lyrics, system media controls (SMTC / MPRIS) and the Windows taskbar player. The command palette also offers quick queue management, volume adjustment and a sleep timer.     Wallpaper Engine support:  Load your Wallpaper Engine library to customize ECHO's video wallpaper, or bring ECHO lyrics onto your desktop.     UltraLight playback:  Unload the main interface while keeping background playback, tray controls and shortcuts. Quick search works without reopening the full interface.     Game mode:  Automatically switch ECHO to a lighter mode while playing other Steam games to reduce memory use. Optional automatic volume adjustment can also change ECHO's volume when another game is detected.    Workshop: shape ECHO your way  Change colors and layouts, or give lyrics and music a new stage. Subscribe to, enable and combine Steam Workshop creations, or start making your own.     Themes and full skins:  Change colors, fonts and controls; full skins can also rearrange pages and playback controls.     Lyric scenes and visualizers:  Choose different lyric layouts, backgrounds and music visuals, combining creations that support independent use.     Functional plugins:  Expand what you can do through commands, tool panels and actions. Plugins declare permissions, and you decide whether to enable and authorize them.     From

short: A strategy roguelike blending bullet hell, inventory management & tower defense. Recruit heroes, merge & evolve, summon goddesses, upgrade your castle, and repel monster waves. 100+ stages, meta progression, low-spec friendly.
about: A brand-new title that's easy to pick up yet packed with strategic depth — blending bullet-hell shooting, inventory management, light Roguelike, and tower defense elements into one addictive experience. name: Dollar Desktop Pet
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: Let AI code. Let Dollar watch. Risky commands are flagged; the irreversible ones stop and ask. An encrypted restore point is taken first, and spending is counted as it happens — all local. Works without AI too: restore points, secret scanning, project checkup. No account, no API key.
about: Fast is great — until it breaks something  AI coding tools can edit files, run commands, and automate whole tasks. That speed is real, and so are the blind spots: a recursive delete runs the moment it is generated, with no second look. One bad edit with no snapshot is just gone. What it cost shows up when the bill does.  Dollar is the local layer that sits next to all of that.  Three things Dollar does   Seatbelt — risky actions speak up before they run.  The default mode flags a risky command as it happens; the genuinely irreversible ones — disk wipes, force-pushing over main, dropping a database, writing credentials — stop and wait for you. Guard mode adds a way back, not another gate: put an agent on Guard and risky actions get their restore point staged first, with a one-click path back right in the notice. Quiet on the safe stuff.   Dashcam — see what your AI did.  A local activity history of flagged actions, approvals and changes, so you can look back instead of guessing.   Black box — recover when it goes wrong.  An encrypted local snapshot is taken before risky changes, so a bad task is one rollback away, not a late-night cleanup.  Works without AI  No account, no API key, no Git required. These work the moment you open it:     Restore points (the vault)  — snapshot a folder, roll it back in one click.     Secret scanning  — find exposed keys before you commit or share. Results are masked.     One-click checkup  — one pass over agent connections, secret scan, project checks and recovery coverage. Produces  one shareable card , and exports a report. Read-only throughout.     Safety range  — see a command's local risk rating (red / yellow / green). Nothing is ever run.     Machine performance and local spend  — the readouts you actually reach for.     A desktop pet  — draggable, pettable, with gentle notifications.  A guardrail you can see is a guardrail you use : Dollar sits on your desktop, not in a background process you forget you installed.    Optional: connect the AI coding agent you already use  If you have a compatible AI coding agent installed, connect it in one click — no commands to copy — and Dollar supervises it live: a heads-up before risky actions, an automatic restore point, and a running tally of what it spends. This layer is optional and separate from the local tools above.  The ledger drills down by  agent, model and month . Each agent reports activity in its own unit (Claude counts messages, Codex counts sessions), and anything with no records shows "—", not 0.  And when you switch agents, switch machines, or a service is temporarily down, the Escape Pod exports a continuity pack you review first — redacted, metadata-only, handed over as a local file. No vendor has to be online.  One-time purchase  $2.99, once. Windows and macOS are both included. No subscription, no account, no Pro tier.  Privacy  Everything runs locally. Zero telemetry, and your project contents are never uploaded. Dollar contains no AI of its own, and its core features need no API key.

name: Pawper: Desktop Pet
lang: English, Portuguese - Brazil, French, Spanish - Spain, Spanish - Latin America
short: A virtual pet that lives on your desktop, not in a window. Pet him, feed him and throw the ball while you work. Clean up his messes for coins, then spend them on toys, outfits and furniture. He grows in real time, ages forever and never dies.
about: He's yours from the day he's born. The whole screen is his home: he picks where to nap, chases the ball between your icons and comes asking for a scratch in the middle of your workday.    Pet him and he stretches, lets out a little heart and squeaks like a rubber toy.    Pawper is a pixel art dog who lives in the same place where you work and play. He never gets in the way, he only reacts when you click on him.         Every real day is a month in your dog's life. He arrives as a puppy and takes  24 real days  to become an adult, going through puppy, teenager and adult, each stage unlocking new items and interactions.    Once he's grown, he keeps aging forever and celebrates every birthday. Time spent with the game closed counts too: he grows while you live your life.         Hunger, thirst, hygiene, energy and happiness run in real time, and his mood changes with the care he gets. But the rules are clear:       Food, water and baths are always free.      Your dog never goes hungry for lack of coins.      Your dog never dies.       The economy exists for progression and fun, never for guilt.            Pick him up:  click and drag to lift him. He floats, spins with the scroll wheel and squashes on landing.     Throw the tennis ball:  it bounces off the edges of your monitor and he runs after it to kick it.     Toss the frisbee:  he fetches it and drops it right at your cursor.     Give him the bone:  he runs to a corner, digs and buries it, until you click to dig it back up.     Drop the bowl on screen:  leave the food on the floor and he'll notice and walk over to it on his own.                      Choose your Pawper at birth:  black, white, golden, akita, german shepherd, border collie, bernese, husky and more, with markings drawn body part by body part.     Dress your dog:  tie, bow, glasses, cap and hat, each with its own colors and alternate styles, like the cap turned backwards or the bow at the tip of his tail.     Decorate your desktop:  dog bed, pee pad, fire hydrant, fences, potted plants, play tunnel and a campfire that really lights up, with flames, warm light and crackling.     Place it however you like:  drag it, spin it with the scroll wheel, and the position stays saved.     Upgrade through three tiers:  the bowl becomes an automatic feeder, the pad and the hydrant clean themselves and collect the coins for you, the bed speeds up his rest and the fence finally holds the little escape artist.           Challenge your own dog without opening anything! Play minigames with your Pawper to raise his happiness and yours too. Always with good rewards so you can make your Pawper more and more your own.    The older the dog, the harder it gets.         A while after eating, he leaves a poop on your screen, and the day still brings the odd puddle of pee. Every mess slowly drains his hygiene: clean it with one click before his mood drops, and earn coins for it.    And the mess respects your time: it stays there waiting for you to come back.           Achievements for care, routine and skill, some of them secret, with milestones that repeat forever.    Retro pixel art interface, a "cozy night" theme and classic arcade typography.    System tray icon, optional floating button and your choice of which monitor he lives on.    Light on CPU and memory: made to stay open all day next to your work.    English, Portuguese (Brazil), French and Spanish, switched at any time without restarting.      Adopt your Pawper and never sit alone again!

about: Welcome to Tokyo Station! The morning rush is about to begin...   "Platform Rush: Tokyo Station" is a lightweight yet strategic 2D pixel-art management simulator. As the station master of one of the busiest hubs in the world, your goal is to expand the station’s concourses, upgrade facilities, and optimize train schedules to ensure thousands of commuters reach their destinations without losing their patience.   【Key Features】      Expand Your Bustling Concourse:  Unlock and expand multiple concourse floors. Build ticket machines and turnstiles, and open Ekiben (bento) stalls, capsule toy (Gashapon) machines, restrooms, and luggage lockers. These facilities generate extra revenue and pacify impatient passengers!     Dynamic Train Dispatching:  Adjust train lengths (up to 6 cars) and dispatch frequencies dynamically, and unlock dual-side tracks. Carefully allocate resources to survive the massive waves of the Morning Rush and Evening Rush.     Handle Unexpected Incidents:  Keep an eye out for sudden "Signal Faults." Tap to repair them quickly before delays cascade and passengers leave the station angry.     A Relaxing "Desktop Pet" Mode:  Want a stress-free experience? Turn on "Casual Sandbox" and shrink the game into a small window. It beautifully transforms into a "Desktop Pet" or an interactive screen companion. While you work, study, or write code, you can passively enjoy watching cute pixel-art passengers wander, buy lunch, play with capsule toys, and watch trains smoothly glide in and out of the station.

name: Shikigami
lang: English*, Japanese*, Simplified Chinese*, Traditional Chinese**
short: A Live2D AI agent who lives on your desktop. Shikigami chats, thinks, and acts — she reads your files, runs commands, plans tasks, and reports back, all while watching you with real-time animation, voice, and a personality you shape. The first desktop companion that actually works for you.
about: Shikigami is a Live2D AI agent who lives on your desktop.   She chats. She thinks. She acts. And she does it all while watching you with eyes that follow your cursor, a voice that's hers, and a personality you shape.  Most "desktop pets" stop at being cute. Most "AI assistants" stop at being a window you have to open. Shikigami is a third thing: a character with real presence and a real autonomous agent under the hood.    >  Bring your own AI.  Shikigami connects to Claude, GPT, Gemini, or any compatible LLM. Pick a TTS engine for her voice. Your keys, your choice. Free local options are on the roadmap.     Lives on Your Desktop        She sits on top of everything — browser, editor, game. Always visible, never blocking. Drag her anywhere. She stays where you put her.     Eyes on You           She tracks your cursor. Looks where you point. Reacts when you click, drag, or pet her head.     She Talks           Real-time TTS with lip-synced animation. Her voice is configurable — swap engines and presets to find the one that fits.     She Thinks        In Chat mode, talk to her about anything. She remembers context, responds with personality, and stays in character.     She Works           In Assistant mode, she becomes your agent. Ask her to find a file, summarize a doc, run git, or plan a multi-step task. She breaks it down, calls tools, executes step by step, and reports back — all through Live2D animation you watch in real time.     Your AI, Your Voice        Claude, GPT, Gemini for the brain. Multiple TTS engines for the voice. Mix, match, swap any time. No vendor lock-in.     Shape Her Soul        Playful, focused, sarcastic, gentle — define who she is. Tune her with presets or write your own prompts. Pick her Live2D model. Pick her voice. Make her yours.     Pomodoro + Sticky Notes        Built-in productivity. She announces your timers. Sticky notes pin to your desktop. Conversation logs you can revisit.     Permission First        She asks for confirmation before any destructive operation. You're always in control.   4 Languages   English, 繁體中文, 简体中文, 日本語. Full UI localization. Voice output via configurable TTS engines.   Low Interruption by Design   She stays quiet when you're focused. Never self-initiates. Never pops up unsolicited. She's there when you want her, invisible when you don't.     Shikigami is where desktop pets and AI tools finally meet — a character with real presence, real personality, and real capability.
